sentences.text: Gobihadros is a medium-sized hadrosauroid dinosaur, a group classified within the superfamily Hadrosauroidea in a basal position outside the family Hadrosauridae.
It is distinguished by a double-layered tomial edge on the premaxilla and up to three teeth per position in the lower jaw, alongside a unique conical, spike-like claw on its first finger.
The largest known fully grown individual reached an estimated length of 7.5 meters.
CT scans of this large individual revealed calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease in its tail vertebrae and foot bones, likely resulting from old age rather than physical trauma.
Life Science Identifiers were required to validate the name Gobihadros because the description was published in an electronic journal.
The species Gobihadros mongoliensis was formally named and described in 2019 by Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, David Bruce Weishampel, David Christopher Evans, and Mahito Watabe.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific example the species is based on, MPC-D100/746, was discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation from the Cenomanian-Santonian stages.
Gobihadros lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
